Which language first, by age

The question every parent and beginner asks. The answer depends on age and goal more than on the language itself, so here it is band by band, with the course that fits.

Ages 6 to 9

Scratch

Blocks teach loops, events and conditions without typing or syntax errors. A child makes a game in the first hour and keeps making them.

Coding for kids trackScratch Coding for Kids courseCoding for 8-year-olds
Ages 10 to 12

Python, with Roblox Luau if games are the hook

Typing is comfortable now and Python reads almost like English. Turtle graphics, then quiz games, then a first AI project. Roblox scripting is real text code with an audience.

Python and AI for Kids courseRoblox Game Coding for KidsPython for 10-year-olds
Ages 13 to 17

Python or JavaScript. Java for ICSE and ISC. C++ for olympiads.

Python if the goal is AI, data or automation. JavaScript if the goal is websites and apps. Board students take the language their exam uses, and olympiad hopefuls go straight to C++.

Coding for teens trackPython for Teens courseJavaScript for Teens courseJava for Teens course
College, 18 and up

Python plus one of C++ or Java

Python for projects, data and AI. C++ or Java for data structures, algorithms and placement interviews. Then pick a stack: web, mobile, AI or systems.

Coding for college students trackPython MasterclassData Structures and Algorithms course
Working professionals

Python for AI, data and automation. JavaScript for the web. Then the AI coding agents.

Most career switchers need one language plus the tools around it. Python covers analytics, automation and AI; JavaScript covers product work. Agents like Claude Code multiply whichever you know.

Coding for professionals trackCodex and Claude Code for ProfessionalsData and AI Analytics for Non-Programmers

Nothing matches that. Try a shorter word, or .

Programming languages

13 entries

Thirteen languages that matter in 2026, in the order most learners meet them. Each entry says what it is for, who it suits, and which of our live courses teaches it.

Python

Language, 3.14

The most recommended first text language. Readable syntax, an enormous library, and the default for AI, data and automation.

Fundamentals
  • Variables and types
  • Functions
  • Lists and dictionaries
  • Object-oriented programming
  • File handling
  • APIs and requests
Used for
AI and machine learning, data science, web backends with Django and FastAPI, automation, scripting, and most school and college curricula.
Who it suits
Kids 10 and up, teens, college students, professionals.

Python 3.14 shipped in October 2025 with an official free-threaded build and template strings. It still tops most 2026 language indexes.

Learn it live with us

JavaScript

Language, ES2025

The only language every browser runs. It powers interactive pages, and through Node.js, servers and developer tools as well.

Fundamentals
  • DOM and events
  • Functions and closures
  • Arrays and objects
  • Async and promises
  • Fetch and JSON
  • ES modules
Used for
Websites and web apps, browser games, Node.js backends, mobile apps with React Native, desktop apps with Electron.
Who it suits
Teens 13 and up, college students, professionals. Kids from about 11 once they know HTML and CSS.

ES2025 added iterator helpers and new Set methods. The same code runs in browsers, Node.js 24, Bun and Deno.

TypeScript

Language, 5.9 and later

JavaScript with types. It catches mistakes before the code runs and is now the default for serious frontend and Node.js work.

Fundamentals
  • Type annotations
  • Interfaces and type aliases
  • Generics
  • Union types and narrowing
  • tsconfig and tooling
Used for
Large web apps, React and Angular codebases, Node.js and NestJS backends, published libraries.
Who it suits
Teens who already know JavaScript, college students, professionals.

The compiler is being ported to Go for builds up to ten times faster. Learn TypeScript after JavaScript, not instead of it.

Language, 25 LTS

C

Language, C23

The small language under everything: operating systems, compilers and microcontrollers. It teaches how memory actually works.

Fundamentals
  • Pointers
  • Arrays and strings
  • Structs
  • Manual memory allocation
  • Compiling and linking
Used for
Operating systems, embedded devices and Arduino, first-year engineering courses, understanding what higher-level languages hide.
Who it suits
College and engineering students, professionals. Teens 15 and up with a specific reason.

Still inside the top ten of every 2026 language index because hardware and operating-system code does not go away.

Learn it live with us

C++

Language, C++23

C with classes, templates and the STL. The language of game engines, competitive programming and anything that must be fast.

Fundamentals
  • Object-oriented programming
  • Pointers and references
  • STL containers
  • Templates
  • Memory management
  • Algorithms
Used for
Game engines such as Unreal, competitive programming, trading systems, browsers, embedded software.
Who it suits
Teens 13 and up heading for olympiads, college students preparing for placements, professionals.

C++23 is the current standard and C++26 is being finalised. It remains the default language at ICPC, Codeforces and INOI.

Go

Language, 1.26

Google's small, fast language for servers and cloud tools. Few features on purpose, so teams read each other's code easily.

Fundamentals
  • Goroutines and channels
  • Interfaces
  • Packages and modules
  • Error handling
  • The standard HTTP library
Used for
Cloud services, DevOps tools (Docker and Kubernetes are written in Go), APIs, command-line tools.
Who it suits
College students and professionals who already know one language.

Go 1.26 keeps the language stable. The growth is in cloud-native and platform engineering jobs.

Rust

Language, 2024 edition

Memory-safe systems programming without a garbage collector. The compiler is strict so that production code does not have to be.

Fundamentals
  • Ownership and borrowing
  • Lifetimes
  • Enums and pattern matching
  • Traits
  • Cargo and crates
Used for
Systems tools, WebAssembly, parts of Linux, Android and Windows, developer tooling, blockchain.
Who it suits
College students and professionals after C or C++. Not a first language.

Rust now ships inside the Linux kernel and Windows, and the 2024 edition is the baseline. We do not run a standalone Rust course; C++ is the closest foundation.

Learn it live with us

C++ Masterclass: Fundamentals to Modern C++ and Systems

Databases and SQL

8 entries

Every app stores data somewhere. SQL is the skill that transfers between all of them, so learn it before choosing a database.

SQL

Query language, SQL:2023

The language for asking questions of data. Every backend developer, analyst and data scientist writes it daily.

Fundamentals

Questions parents and learners ask

What is the best programming language to learn first in 2026?

Python, for most people. Its syntax reads almost like English, it powers AI, data science and automation, and it is what most school and college syllabi use. Choose JavaScript instead if your goal is websites and web apps. Children under about 10 should start with Scratch, a visual block language, and move to Python once typing is comfortable.

Which coding language should my child start with, by age?

Ages 6 to 9: Scratch. Ages 10 to 12: Python, with Roblox Luau if games are the motivation. Ages 13 to 17: Python or JavaScript, Java if they are an ICSE or ISC student, and C++ if they are aiming at programming olympiads. Modern Age Coders runs live courses for every one of these bands, and the age table on this page links to each.

Which programming languages and frameworks are most in demand in 2026?

Python, JavaScript and TypeScript lead general demand. React and Next.js dominate the frontend, with Angular strong in enterprises. Node.js, Django, FastAPI and Spring Boot cover the backend. PostgreSQL and MongoDB are the common databases. PyTorch, scikit-learn and the large language model APIs from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google cover AI. Docker, Kubernetes and AWS cover cloud. Go and Rust keep rising for systems and cloud-native work, and AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot are now part of most job descriptions.

Do AI coding agents like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot make learning to code pointless?

No. Agents write more of the code, but someone still has to specify what to build, judge whether the output is correct, fix what breaks and take responsibility for security and performance. Every one of those needs the fundamentals: how data structures work, how the web works, how to read code. Our AI coding agents courses teach the tools on top of that foundation rather than instead of it.

Should I learn the language first or jump straight to a framework?

Learn the language first: variables, functions, loops, data structures and object-oriented basics. Then a framework such as React for JavaScript or Django for Python lets you build complete applications much faster. Frameworks change every few years; the fundamentals stay valuable for a whole career.

How long does it take to learn a programming language?

Most learners build a first working project within four to eight weeks of steady practice. Reaching the point where you can build a full application on your own usually takes six to twelve months with structured, project-based teaching. Our courses run ten to fourteen months for exactly that reason, with two live classes a week and projects in every phase.

Are Modern Age Coders classes live or recorded, and how big are the batches?

Every class is live and online with a mentor, never a pre-recorded video. You can choose 1-on-1 classes, a mini batch of three to four learners, or a group of five to ten. Every course is project-based and awards a certificate on passing the final exam. Book a free demo class to see the format before enrolling.

Do you teach every technology listed on this page?

Every entry links to the course that covers it, and the free tutorial library where one exists. For a small number of technologies, such as Rust, Ruby, PHP, Kubernetes and Terraform, we do not run a standalone course. Those entries point to the closest foundation course, and you can tell us your goal on the form; a mentor will say honestly whether a 1-on-1 plan makes sense.
